citation.authors: Krishnan S, Rosenberg L, Singer M, Hu FB et al

cited_by.title: Plantain, yam and cassava: blood sugar and safety

record.population: About 59,000 US Black women in the Black Women's Health Study, 8 years' follow-up, 1,938 new cases of diabetes
record.design: Prospective cohort study with food-frequency questionnaire
record.finding: Women in the highest fifth for dietary glycaemic index had 23% higher diabetes rates than the lowest fifth (IRR 1.23, 95% CI 1.05 to 1.44), and women in the highest fifth for cereal fibre had 18% lower (IRR 0.82). Associations were stronger in women with a BMI under 25.
record.note: Observational, self-reported diet; one cohort; it does not say which individual staples drive the result.
